problem.text: How many ordered pairs $(a,b)$ of positive integers satisfy the equation $$a\cdot b+63=20\cdot\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)+12\cdot\gcd(a,b),$$ where $\gcd(a,b)$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$, and $\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$ denotes their least common multiple?

steps.title: Where to start: write $a\cdot b$ with the gcd and lcm
steps.body:
The equation mixes $ab$ with the gcd and lcm, so try to write everything using only $g=\gcd(a,b)$ and $L=\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)$. Write $a=gm$ and $b=gn$, where $m$ and $n$ share no common factor (otherwise $g$ would not be the greatest). Then the lcm is $L=gmn$, so
$$ab=g^2mn=g\cdot gmn=g\cdot L.$$

your_turn.prompt: Rewrite the equation using only $g$ and $L$.

steps.title: Factor it
steps.body: Move everything to one side: $gL-20L-12g=-63$. This looks like part of the product $(L-12)(g-20)=gL-20L-12g+240$. Adding $240$ to both sides completes that product; this trick is often called Simon's Favorite Factoring Trick.

your_turn.prompt: What does the equation become? Factor the number on the right into primes.

steps.title: Find the possible $(L,g)$
steps.body: Both factors must be positive: if both were negative, $g-20$ and $L-12$ would be negative divisors of $177$, and in every such case $g$ or $L$ comes out negative. So $(L-12,\,g-20)$ is one of $(1,177)$, $(3,59)$, $(59,3)$, $(177,1)$. Careful: $g$ and $L$ are not free numbers, because the gcd of two numbers always divides their lcm.

your_turn.prompt: List the four pairs $(L,g)$. Which one has $g$ dividing $L$?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: So $g=21$ and $L=189$. With $a=21m$, $b=21n$ and $L=21mn$, we need $mn=9$ with $m$ and $n$ sharing no factor. That allows $(m,n)=(1,9)$ or $(9,1)$ but not $(3,3)$, giving $(a,b)=(21,189)$ and $(189,21)$. Check: $21\cdot189+63=4032=20\cdot189+12\cdot21$. There are $2$ ordered pairs. The answer is **(B)**.

wrong_choices.C: $4$ comes from counting all four factor pairs of $177$ as solutions. Only one of them has the gcd dividing the lcm, so the other three give no actual numbers $a$ and $b$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
